claims.text: Scope figure: DSS 'monitors whether 11,000-plus contractor facilities' security programs meet NISP requirements.' GAO found DSS could not demonstrate that its oversight reduced the risk of compromise and issued seven recommendations, including establishing results-oriented performance goals, identifying information needed to detect systemic vulnerabilities, regular trend analysis, time-based criteria for compromise determinations and notifications, and accountability mechanisms for identifying the government customer.

sources.title: GAO-04-332 - Industrial Security: DOD Cannot Provide Adequate Assurances That Its Oversight Ensures the Protection of Classified Information

claims.text: GAO-04-332 audited the very oversight function that the carve-out provision switches off. Its finding that DSS could not assure adequate oversight of the 11,000+ facilities it DID inspect is a floor, not a ceiling, for facilities where a SecDef/DepSecDef carve-out had removed DSS entirely -- those sites are outside the population GAO could even sample. Reasoning stated. GAO's own SAP access is separately gated by DoDI 5205.11 para 7.2.g.

desc: Requested in response to a Senate report accompanying the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004, GAO-04-332 assessed the Defense Security Service's oversight of more than 11,000 cleared contractor facilities under the National Industrial Security Program and DSS's actions after possible compromises of classified information. Its title is its finding. For this board the most important sentence is a footnote: 'As agreed with committee staff, our review was limited to DSS's oversight of contractor facilities' protection of Confidential, Secret, and Top Secret information as defined in Executive Order no. 12958, as amended, and did not include DSS's oversight of special access programs at contractor facilities.' GAO then explains, in unclassified text, what a SAP is: programs 'established to provide protection for particularly sensitive classified information beyond that normally required for Top Secret, Secret, or Confidential information'. The report is the cleanest available demonstration of the structural point: the legislative branch's own auditor, auditing the security of contractor facilities holding classified material, was steered away from the compartment where the most sensitive material sits, and did so by agreement with the committee that asked for the audit. Every subsequent claim that 'GAO has looked at this' has to contend with that footnote.

entityInfo.desc: The audit that was steered. When officials say the special access program system is subject to oversight, the honest test is to ask what the Government Accountability Office has actually examined. GAO-04-332 is the only public GAO product on the security of cleared contractor facilities under the National Industrial Security Program. It was requested by the Senate in the report accompanying the FY2004 NDAA. It found that DoD could not provide adequate assurances that its oversight ensures the protection of classified information, and that DSS had not always followed required procedures after reported compromises. And its second footnote records that, 'As agreed with committee staff', the review deliberately excluded DSS's oversight of special access programs at contractor facilities. The auditor was sent into the building and asked not to open one set of doors - by agreement with the committee that commissioned the audit. Every subsequent assertion that the contractor SAP system has been independently examined has to be measured against that sentence.
